title: Learner UI/UX Competitive Parity and Polished Cross-Platform Study Experience

preflight.note: Created from the 2026-09-11 competitive product review before a broad visual/interaction redesign begins. SkillForge already has a coherent React/Tauri study product; this work closes discoverability, cross-platform interaction, perceived polish, accessibility, and real-learner usability gaps without copying competitor design or weakening the app's offline-first/no-account posture.

acceptance_criteria.text: Publish a task-based UX parity study of representative current certification-prep products using only public/product-observable behavior. Compare first-run/start-study flow, resume/next-action guidance, objective browsing, custom practice, mock exams, PBQs, flashcards, bookmarks/notes, search, weak-area targeting, analytics, settings, backup/restore, and mobile behavior. Record friction and useful patterns without copying protected visual design or content.

Define and apply one coherent SkillForge design system for typography, spacing, density, surfaces, controls, data visualization, status/feedback, focus/selection, dialog/sheet behavior, touch targets, desktop pointer behavior, dark/light themes, and semantic states. The system supports desktop and mobile rather than treating mobile as a scaled-down desktop screenshot.

Reconcile information architecture and navigation around learner intent. A learner can quickly answer: what should I study next, how ready am I and why, what am I weak on, how do I practice one objective/domain, how do I take a realistic exam, what did I miss, and how do I resume unfinished work. Advanced analytics remain available without making the primary study path cognitively heavy.

Improve onboarding and return-session behavior with a bounded first-run walkthrough, certification/goal selection, clear local-data/no-account explanation, and a useful default next action. Returning learners resume meaningful context without being forced through repeated prompts, and zero-history/empty states teach the workflow instead of appearing unfinished.

Make practice, PBQ, flashcard, and mock-exam interaction states fully polished: selected/unselected answers, multi-select limits, validation, timer behavior, pause/exit confirmation where applicable, keyboard/touch input, feedback timing, explanations, bookmarking/notes, partial credit, completion review, retry/drill actions, and accidental-navigation protection are consistent and tested.

Make analytics and readiness explanations actionable rather than decorative. Charts/heatmaps have accessible labels and textual equivalents, drill-down reaches the underlying objective/evidence, weak-area recommendations explain their basis, insufficient-data states are explicit, and color alone is never required to interpret mastery or risk.

Close responsive/mobile interaction gaps across supported Tauri targets: safe areas, orientation/viewport changes, virtual keyboard behavior, scrolling and sticky controls, dialogs/sheets, back navigation, touch hit targets, long content, chart readability, offline launch, and process/lifecycle resume are tested on real or supported emulator/device paths. Desktop-specific shortcuts remain enhancements, not prerequisites for core workflows.

Meet a manual accessibility acceptance gate in addition to automated checks. Run keyboard-only walkthroughs of every major workflow and screen-reader walkthroughs with NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver when macOS/iOS evidence becomes available; record focus order, announcements, dynamic updates, error handling, dialog containment, reduced-motion/high-contrast behavior, and unresolved limitations.

Establish perceived-performance gates for startup, navigation, question advance, search, large question/lesson lists, analytics rendering, backup/restore feedback, and track switching. Expensive operations expose progress or remain off the interaction-critical path; no animation or polish work may hide blocked input or stale state. Record representative low/mid-range hardware results.

Add automated screenshot/visual-regression and interaction-state coverage for the highest-value desktop and responsive views using deterministic demo state. Baselines cover empty, populated, loading where applicable, error/degraded, completed/review, and theme states while allowing deliberate design updates through reviewed baseline changes.

Run a small real-learner usability pilot before declaring UX parity. Preserve task-completion observations, time/friction, navigation mistakes, misunderstood labels/metrics, accessibility feedback, and qualitative preference notes. Fix or explicitly disposition high-severity findings; maintainer familiarity and screenshot aesthetics do not substitute for learner evidence.

Preserve SkillForge's product advantages through the redesign: core study remains account-free, offline-capable, telemetry-free by default, locally owned, and transparent about backup/data handling. Competitive polish may add optional conveniences but cannot make a hosted account, advertising/engagement loop, or opaque cloud recommendation service a prerequisite for ordinary learning.
